question.text: Neelgiri AIF has 55% of its corpus contributed by LPs whose beneficial owners are citizens of China. Under SEBI's Oct 8, 2024 circular on Specific Due Diligence (referencing Rule 6 of FEMA NDI Rules), when must the AIF report its investments to the Custodian?

answer.text: No reporting is required if the investors are passive LPs

Specific DD must be conducted before making any investment; any investment where the scheme holds ≥10% of equity/equity-linked securities of an investee (fully diluted) must be reported to Custodian within 30 days of investment

explanation.text: The Logic: Specific due diligence must be conducted before making investments where 50% or more of the AIF scheme's corpus is contributed by investors (or beneficial owners) from land-border-sharing countries. Where investments cause the scheme to hold 10% or more of an investee's equity or equity-linked securities (fully diluted), the scheme must report to its Custodian within 30 days of investment. The Trap: Option A defers reporting to annual audit (too late). Option B ignores active DD obligations. Option C is reactive; proactive DD is mandated. Note: Workbook pages 367 and 369-370 contain the October 8, 2024 specific-DD framework and the 30-day land-border reporting rule.
